notes:
CIRCUIT: a five-MOSFET network (two N-channel, three P-channel) between a +5 V top rail and a common ground rail, with a 3 V zener, a 1 kOhm resistor, and four independent sources (1 V/2 kHz and 5 V/3 kHz AC voltage sources, 1 A/2 kHz and 5 A/3 kHz AC current sources) driving various nodes. The 5 V V-DC #0 sits between the top rail and GND #2, so the top rail is the supply. 14 components, 8 nets.

NET MAP:
  n1 = the top rail, y~282, x 118..510, plus the two stubs down to the MOSFET drains: zener #4 top (4.0), #3 drain (3.0), #1 drain (1.0), V-DC #0 left terminal (0.0).
  0  = ground. Two disjoint drawn pieces both carrying a GND symbol: (a) V-DC #0's right lead (591,282) running right to GND #2 (0.1, 2.0); (b) the bottom rail y~695..720, x 190..920, with GND #13 hanging off it at (549,705): #6 V-AC bottom (6.1), #8 source (8.2), I-AC #9 bottom (9.1), #10 source (10.2), #11 V-AC bottom (11.1), I-AC #12 bottom (12.1), GND #13 (13.0). Both pieces are net '0' because every GND symbol is net 0 by definition.
  n2 = the gate rail. #1's gate lead runs left from (372,350) to (335,390); the column at x~330 then drops, hopping over the y~392 wire at S6 and over the y~492 wire at S10, down to (323,559) where #11 V-AC's top lead arrives from the left (S15), and continues down and right to #8's gate lead at (391,633): 1.1, 8.1, 11.0. So the 5 V/3 kHz source drives both N-channel gates.
  n3 = the horizontal at y~392 from #3's source column (262,391) rightwards past the S6 hop to #1's source column (425,390), then the y~396 wire running right to #5's drain (667,397): 1.2, 3.2, 5.0.
  n4 = zener #4 bottom (118,387) down to S8 (116,434), right along y~433 to S7 (191,433) where #3's gate lead comes down from (206,368), on to (238,433), down to (238,492), right along y~492 (passing UNDER the gate column at S10) to (434,494), then to S13 (438,549) where #8's drain lead arrives from below and the 1 kOhm resistor's left lead starts; #6 V-AC's top lead also hangs on the S8 column: 3.1, 4.1, 6.0, 7.0, 8.0.
  n5 = #5's gate lead running right from (734,462) to x~917, then down to I-AC #9's top terminal: 5.1, 9.0.
  n6 = #5's source column down from (664,480) to S14 (664,554), where the 1 kOhm resistor's right lead arrives from the left, continuing down to #10's drain lead (664,571): 5.2, 7.1, 10.0.
  n7 = #10's gate lead running right from (736,634), then round and down to I-AC #12's top terminal (845,603): 10.1, 12.0.

CRITICAL SITES (explicit decisions):
  S1 (253,282) -> JUNCTION. T where #3's drain column meets the top rail; nothing continues above. Crossing would strand #3's drain.
  S2 (421,283) -> JUNCTION. Same, for #1's drain column; the top rail continues right to V-DC #0.
  S4 (428,390) -> JUNCTION. T where #1's source column lands on the y~392 wire.
  S5 (262,391) -> JUNCTION. T where #3's source column lands on the y~392 wire.
  S6 (335,392) -> CROSSING. The crop shows an unmistakable S-shaped sideways jog: the gate column comes down at x~334, steps right, passes the y~392 horizontal, and steps back left (hop_score 34.1, dot only 1.8). edges.py confirms the tracer's opposite-branch pairing is right: e15+e16 are the two halves of the y~392 wire, e10+e18 are the gate column above and below. Junction would merge the two N-gates and the 5 V/3 kHz source into n3 (the sources of #1 and #3 and the drain of #5), i.e. it would tie #1's own gate to its own source.
  S7 (191,433) -> JUNCTION. Solder blob (dot=2.1) where #3's gate lead comes down onto the y~433 wire, which continues left to the zener column and right toward the y~492 run. Crossing would cut #3's gate off from the zener node.
  S8 (116,434) -> JUNCTION. T where the y~433 wire lands on the zener/#6 column. Crossing would split the zener's bottom from the 1 V source and from #3's gate.
  S10 (332,492) -> CROSSING. Same S-jog as S6, one column lower (hop_score 45.0). Branch pairing verified with edges.py: e24+e25 are the two halves of the y~492 wire (part of n4), e18+e26 are the gate column. Junction here would merge the gate net n2 into n4, tying #8's gate to #8's own drain and to the zener node.
  S13 (438,549) -> JUNCTION. Fattest blob on the sheet (dot=2.5): #8's drain column comes up, the y~492 run comes in from the left/above, and the 1 kOhm resistor's left lead leaves to the right.
  S14 (664,554) -> JUNCTION. T where the resistor's right lead lands on the column running from #5's source down to #10's drain.
  S15 (324,562) -> JUNCTION. T where #11 V-AC's top lead arrives from the left onto the gate column, which continues down to #8's gate.
  S35 (252,693), S36 (441,699), S38 (664,713), S39 (839,720) -> JUNCTION. Four clean Ts where #11's bottom, #8's source, #10's source and I-AC #12's bottom land on the bottom (ground) rail.
  S37 (549,705) -> JUNCTION. The bottom rail with the short stub down to GND #13. hop=1.4 is the rail's slight sag, not an arc; crossing would leave GND #13 on a one-terminal net.
  Non-critical sites left at default: S12, S17, S18, S20, S21, S23, S24, S26, S29, S31, S32 - all of them are strokes of the handwritten labels ('1kOhm', '1A 2kHz', '5v 3kHz', '5A 3kHz', '5V') brushing wires or source circles.

PORT / PIN-ORDER FIXES:
  #0 V-DC t1 -> port p3 (591,282). The tracer had t1 on p1 (556,320), an 11 px stroke of the handwritten '5V' under the source circle, which left n2 with a single terminal. p3 is the real right-hand lead (88 px) running across to GND #2.
  #9 I-AC t0 -> port p4 (921,565). The tracer had t0 on p3 (951,581), a 4 px stroke of the handwritten '1A'. p4 is the real top lead (283 px) that runs up the far-right column and across to #5's gate. This fixed two one-terminal nets at once (the old n7 = #5's gate alone and n8 = #9 alone).
  MOSFET pin order (drain, gate, source) - the drafter draws every FET the same way: a long gate bar with its lead on one side, three channel segments on the other, and three leads off the channel. The middle lead carries the body arrow and always runs into the SAME corner wire as the BOTTOM lead, so the bottom lead is the source and the top lead is the drain in all five. Arrow directions confirm the channel type: #1 and #8 (gate bar on the left) have the arrow pointing left, into the channel = N-channel; #3 (gate bar on the left) has it pointing right, away from the channel = P-channel; #5 and #10 are drawn MIRRORED (gate bar on the right, leads running left) and their arrows point left, i.e. again away from the gate = P-channel. All five agree with the annotated classes.
    #1 MOSFET-N: t0=p2 top DRAIN (unchanged), t1=p0 left GATE (was p1), t2=p1 bottom SOURCE (was p0).
    #5 MOSFET-P (mirrored): t0=p0 top DRAIN (unchanged), t1=p2 right GATE (was p1), t2=p1 bottom SOURCE (was p2).
    #10 MOSFET-P (mirrored): t0=p1 top DRAIN (unchanged), t1=p2 right GATE (was p0), t2=p0 bottom SOURCE (was p2).
    #3 MOSFET-P and #8 MOSFET-N were already drain/gate/source and are left untouched (verified at 10x on both).

OTHER WARNINGS CHECKED: the remaining 'unused port candidate' warnings on #7 (545,533)/(513,535), #11 (284,634)/(280,657)/(280,645) and #12 (855,666) are all strokes of the '1kOhm', '5v 3kHz' and '5A 3kHz' labels; the assigned ports are the genuine leads. All 28 gap bridges were non-critical and are kept as found.

CLASSES: all 14 accepted. The '3V' symbol is a zener (bent bar) - correct; #6 and #11 are plain sine-in-a-circle V-AC; #9 and #12 are sine-plus-arrow-in-a-circle I-AC (consistent with their '1A' and '5A' labels); #0 is a circle with + and - (V-DC).

UNRESOLVED: nothing. Note for the auditor that ground appears as two physically separate pieces of ink (V-DC #0's right lead into GND #2, and the bottom rail into GND #13) with no drawn wire between them; both are net '0' per the GND rule, which is also the only reading that gives the circuit a return path.
